question: Where is the National Research Centre of Agroforestry (NRCAF) located?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Jhansi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **National Research Centre of Agroforestry (NRCAF)** is located in **Jhansi, Uttar Pradesh, India**.
 
• The institute was established in **1988** under the **Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR)** to promote and conduct research in the field of agroforestry.
 
• NRCAF is dedicated to developing **agroforestry technologies** that are sustainable, environmentally friendly, and beneficial for farmers.
 
• The location in **Jhansi** was chosen due to its unique agro-climatic conditions, making it suitable for studying agroforestry models applicable to dry and semi-arid regions.
 
• NRCAF focuses on integrating **trees, crops, and livestock** in sustainable land-use systems to improve productivity, reduce soil degradation, and enhance rural livelihoods.
 
• The research center also plays a critical role in addressing issues related to **climate change** and **ecological balance** through agroforestry innovations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Significance of Agroforestry:**

 
 
• **Agroforestry** is a land management system that integrates **trees and shrubs** into agricultural landscapes.
 
• It is recognized as a sustainable practice to address issues like **soil erosion, biodiversity loss, and climate change**.
 
• Agroforestry improves **soil fertility** by fixing nitrogen, provides **shade and shelter** to crops, and enhances **carbon sequestration**, making it an essential tool in combating global warming.
 
 
 
• **Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR):**
 
 
• **ICAR** is an autonomous organization under the **Department of Agricultural Research and Education (DARE)**, Ministry of Agriculture, Government of India.
 
• Founded in **1929**, ICAR plays a pivotal role in coordinating agricultural education and research in India.
 
• It oversees institutes like NRCAF to ensure research focuses on improving agricultural productivity and sustainability.
 
 
 
• **Other Agroforestry Research Centers in India:**
 
 
• While NRCAF is the **national-level** center for agroforestry, state-level research centers and agricultural universities also contribute to agroforestry research and development.
 
• For example, the **Central Soil and Water Conservation Research and Training Institute** in Dehradun and the **Tropical Agroforestry Research Station** in Kerala focus on region-specific agroforestry practices.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Role of NRCAF:**

 
 
• NRCAF works on developing region-specific **agroforestry models** to suit the diverse agro-climatic zones in India.
 
• It conducts training programs and workshops to educate farmers, researchers, and policymakers about the benefits and practices of agroforestry.
 
• The center collaborates with international organizations to implement **global agroforestry initiatives** in India.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Agroforestry:**
 
 
• Agroforestry systems have demonstrated significant benefits in terms of **environmental conservation**, **enhanced agricultural productivity**, and **poverty alleviation**.
 
• These systems are particularly beneficial for small and marginal farmers in regions like Jhansi, where NRCAF is actively working.
